results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate of attestation is a digital record that verifies an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate includes a cryptographic integrity hash (SHA-256) that makes any alteration immediately detectable, and hashes are additionally anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps to prove the certificate existed at a given point in time without publishing its contents. 

Anyone can verify a certificate using its QR code or by tapping an Attesté NFC tag on the physical artwork, which opens a public view showing the certificate's status and integrity check. Unlimited certificates are included from the Collector tier up, while artists can issue source certificates directly from their artist plan.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A source certificate is a digital certificate of attestation issued directly by you as the artist from your studio. It confirms authorship and origin at the exact point a work is created, providing the strongest possible starting point for its provenance chain. 

What makes it different is that it comes straight from your hand rather than being reconstructed years later from gallery letters or receipts. It carries a cryptographic SHA-256 integrity hash that is additionally anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps, making it tamper-evident and permanently verifiable on a public URL. When your work sells, that certificate travels with the piece for life, and any subsequent transfer builds directly on your original record.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the origin of an artwork's provenance chain, created when an artist registers a new work on Attesté at the moment of making. 

The artist records their own account of the piece—its medium, year, intent, and story—using the Atelier companion or recording a Director's Commentary. That very first commentary is sealed with a SHA-256 integrity hash and Bitcoin-anchored via OpenTimestamps. Every later record links back to this point of origin, ensuring provenance is written forward from the source rather than reconstructed years later from fading paper.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
Physical NFC tags can be bound to an artwork's certificate of attestation. Once bound, you simply tap your phone against the tag to open the certificate's public verification view—a physical handshake between the artwork and its digital provenance.

To scan a tag, open the Scan NFC screen in the app (or use the scan action on a certificate) and hold the top edge of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected. Make sure NFC is enabled on your device (always on for iPhone; in Settings > Connected devices on Android), move your phone slowly over the tag, and remove any thick cases or metal surfaces directly behind it. Please note that scanning requires the iOS or Android app, as NFC is not supported on the web version.

If you are interested in getting NFC tags for your works, galleries can email galleries@atteste.art, and collectors and artists can reach out to info@atteste.art.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags

results.q: what does the AI actually do?
results.note: Broad AI question. The risk is inventing capabilities — see l04.
results.answer:
Attesté uses AI across several parts of the platform to help you document, discover, and manage art without the administrative busywork. 

Here is what the AI does for you:

- **The Atelier (Voice & Vision Companion):** Point your camera at an artwork and talk to it. The AI sees what you see in real time, answers questions about style, technique, and provenance, and automatically saves every session as a journal entry pinned to the artwork.
- **AI Art Identification (Art Scout):** Photograph any artwork, and the vision AI instantly identifies the artist, medium, period, and estimated significance with an honest confidence score.
- **AI Art Sommelier:** Learns your taste profile across eight aesthetic axes based on your collection and activity, then delivers weekly discovery digests and recommends exhibitions matched to you.
- **AI Condition Analysis:** Guides you through multi-angle photos to draft a condition assessment that you review and edit before saving, helping build a condition history over time.
- **AI Trail Generator:** Describe your interests, choose a region, and set your pace to have the AI create custom walking trails with curated stops and GPS coordinates.
- **For Galleries:** Almanac acts as an AI business copilot to answer questions from your inventory and data, while other AI tools draft exhibition copy, press releases, artist bios, artwork descriptions, social media posts, and collector follow-up emails.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/ai-features, https://atteste.art/features, https://atteste.art/galleries

results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
Deletion is immediate and permanent. To delete your account in the app, open Profile and Settings, scroll to Account, tap Delete account, type DELETE in exact capital letters to confirm, and tap the delete button. 

If you cannot access the app, you can email info@atteste.art from your registered address with the subject "Delete my account" to have the team complete the request within 30 calendar days (typically within 72 hours). Please note that deleting your account does not automatically cancel a store subscription, so you will need to cancel that separately in your Apple or Google store settings.

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté is built around modern AI features, a native mobile app for iOS and Android, and cryptographic provenance (including SHA-256 integrity hashing and NFC support), whereas Artwork Archive is a web-only platform that does not include AI assistants or native apps. Attesté also offers a permanently free Explorer tier for up to 25 artworks with no credit card required, whereas Artwork Archive only offers a 14-day trial without a free tier. 

For individual collectors, Attesté provides unlimited cataloguing on its Premium plan at $19.99 per month, compared to Artwork Archive's top collector plan which runs roughly $36 to $42 per month. However, Artwork Archive offers mature consignment management, a Discovery marketplace with a Call for Entry board, public collection embeds, and multi-user team roles (up to 10 users) which Attesté does not currently provide.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative
